Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:19352
Court No. - 71
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 107 of 2025

Applicant :- Neeraj Yadav And 2 Others
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Abhishek Ankur Chaurasia,Diwan Saifullah Khan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1.
Heard Mr. D.S. Khan, the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State.
2. Perused the record.

3. Applicants, who are charge sheeted accused, have approached this Court by means of present application under section 482 Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
" It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble court may kindly be pleased to allow this application and quash the impugned charge sheet dated Neeraj Yadav And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4773768/
1 24.07.2023 submitted against the applicant no. 1 in case crime No. 305 of 2023 under section 328, 376, 377, 354z, 452, 342, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C., and against the applicant no. 2 & 3 under section 323, 506, I.P.C Police Station- Kasganj, District- Kasganj as well as cognizance and summoning order dated 03.08.2024 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kasganj, so that justice may be done.

It is further prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to stay the further proceedings of the Case No. 7116 of 2024 (State Vs. Neera Yadav and others arising out of Case crime no. 305 of 2023, U/s 328, 376, 377, 3544, 452, 342, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station- Kasganj, District- Kasganj, so that justice may be done.
And / or may be pleased to pass any other order or direction which this Hon'ble court may deem fit and proper in the present fact and circumstances of the case."
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicants submits that though applicants are named and charge sheeted accused, however, in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, as have emerged on record, the impugned proceedings cannot be sustained.
Consequently, the same are liable to be quashed by this Court.

5. In furtherance of aforesaid submission, the learned counsel for applicants submits that prior to the F.I.R. dated 4.5.2023, lodged by the prosecutrix/first informant/opposite party-2, she had solemnized marriage with applicant-1 on 15.9.2020.
Consequently, by reason of above, the prosecutrix became the legally wedded wife of applicant-1.
Resultantly, the prosecutrix started living with applicant-1 as his legally wedded wife.
The bonafide of the parties is further evident from the fact that the marriage of parties has been registered under the provisions of the U.P. Registration of Marriage Rules, 2017.
Photocopy of the same is on record and is at page 49 of the paper book.

He,
thereforefurther, contends that no proceedings have been initiated by the prosecutrix/first informant/opposite party-2 for declaration of her marriage with applicant-1 as void on the ground of fraud etc.

Since the marriage of the parties is duly registered under aforementioned Rules, therefore,
there is a statutory presumption regarding valid and legal marriage of the parties.
The prosecutrix is major.
She has willingly and knowingly solemnized marriage with applicant-1.
On the above premise, it is thus contended by the learned counsel for applicants that no offence under section 376 IPC can be said to have been committed.
In view of above, the allegations made qua other offences is also unsustainable.
He, therefore, submits that present criminal prosecution of applicants is not only malicious but also an abuse of the process of Court.

6. According to the learned counsel for applicants, the FIR giving rise to present criminal proceedings was lodged by the prosecutrix/first informant/opposite party-2 after expiry of a period of two years and three months from the date of marriage of the prosecutrix with applicant-1.
As such, the F.I.R. is highly belated.

However, no explanation has come forward from prosecutrix/first informant/opposite party-2 in the FIR itself explaining the delay/laches in lodging the F.I.R.
7.

Subsequent to the above FIR, the statements of the prosecutrix were recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., copies of which are on record as Annexures-6 and 7 to the affidavit filed in support Neeraj Yadav And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4773768/
2 of present application.

entities.text: Neeraj Yadav And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, even in the aforesaid statements also, no explanation has come forward regarding the delay in lodging the FIR.
It is thus urged that the delay in lodging the FIR remains unexplained.

8. Referring to paragraph 5 of the judgement of Supreme Court in Shivendra Pratap Singh Thakur @
Banti Vs. State of Chhattisgarh and Others, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 938, the learned counsel for applicants submits that the Apex Court, in aforementioned case, quashed the proceedings against accused therein on account of unexplained delay of 39 days in lodging the F.I.R.

entities.text:
Shivendra Pratap Singh Thakur @
Banti Vs. State of Chhattisgarh and Others, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 938
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the above conspectus, he, therefore, submits that present application is also liable to be allowed.
9. Per contra, the learned A.G.A representing State-opposite party-1 has opposed the present application.
However, he could not dislodge the legal submission urged by the learned counsel for applicants with reference to the record at this stage.
10. Having heard the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State and upon perusal of record, this Court finds that the matter requires consideration.
11. Notice on behalf of opposite party - 1 has been accepted by learned A.G.A.

12. Issue notice to opposite party -2.
13.
All the opposite parties may file their respective counter affidavits on or before the date fixed in the notice.
14. List for admission on 24.3.2025 15.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the submissions urged by learned counsel for applicants as noted herein above, as an interim measure, it is, hereby, provided that till the next date of listing, further proceedings in Case No. 7116 of 2024 (State Vs. Neera Yadav and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 305 of 2023, under Sections 328, 376, 377, 3544, 452, 342,
323, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station- Kasganj, District- Kasganj now pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kasganj, shall remain stayed.
Order Date :- 10.2.2025 Arshad  Neeraj Yadav And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4773768/
